endorsements.title: Marketing Submission Recommendations for a Predetermined Change Control Plan for AI-Enabled Device Software Functions (final guidance)
endorsements.quote: Specifically, the public facing document include information about the PCCP as appropriate, including a summary of the plan modification, testing methods, validation activities, and performance requirements to be met in order for modifications to be implemented, and means by which users will be informed of device modifications implemented in accordance with the authorized PCCP.

endorsements.title: The fairness paradox in public regulatory summaries of FDA-authorized artificial intelligence-enabled medical devices
endorsements.quote: FDA guidance on predetermined change control plans (PCCPs) further recommends a description of modifications, modification protocol, and impact assessment, together with public-facing information about planned modifications, testing, validation, performance requirements, and communication to users ( 27 ).

commentary.bottom_line: No study supplied to this map tests whether public summaries of authorized predetermined change control plans help users anticipate or evaluate model changes. The recommendation rests on FDA final guidance and one commentary, both of which call for such disclosure.

perspectives.view: The map lists zero studies testing the practice and zero studies documenting the hazard. The two endorsements are a guidance document and a commentary, which record expert and regulatory expectation rather than measured effects. Under GRADE conventions, no body of evidence exists to rate, so the effect of disclosure on user understanding or patient outcomes remains unknown.

FDA final guidance on predetermined change control plans recommends that the public-facing document summarize planned modifications, testing methods, validation activities, performance requirements, and how users will be informed. The commentary restates these elements. The guidance uses recommending language, so disclosure depends on developer uptake, and neither source reports how often or how completely summaries are published.

commentary.research_gap: Studies could measure how often authorized plans have public summaries, how complete they are against the elements the FDA guidance lists, and whether clinicians and health system staff who read them can correctly predict how a model's behavior will change after an update. Studies could also test whether disclosure changes local revalidation practice or detection of performance shifts after modifications.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Whether public change summaries are usable by safety-net systems with limited technical staff, or reach patients with limited English proficiency or low literacy, has not been examined.
